short_desc: Open World world_data/ dir empty - no save files for 44+ days
long_desc:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND (2026-06-02 22:12): open-world-selena/src/main.rs save logic is only triggered on explicit REST API calls (POST /api/world/save, update_world, world/create with generate_sample=true). The entity_action handler at line 1149 (the path used by the API server scheduler) does NOT call save_world. Additionally, the auto_save_interval_secs field (default 300s) on the World struct is never read anywhere in main.rs - no auto-save loop exists. So even though the scheduler has run 55+ times today ticking the World Clock, world_data/save.owbl is never written. Stale PID file data/open_world.pid (currently 3298, real PID 4904) means restarts also don't propagate the new PID to the api server's tracker. Older sibling project open-world/ (no -selena) has save.owbl from Apr 18 - confirms save logic worked at some point, broken in the fork/refactor. FIX OPTIONS: (A) Add save_world call to end of entity_action; (B) Implement the missing auto_save_interval_secs loop in main (spawn task that checks elapsed time); (C) Add save call to scheduled_actions.py in selena-project after each cycle. Option B is cleanest, matches the existing setting. Sibling: in_progress todo 781c6ec5 'Investigate Open World frequent crashes' (P8) - this persistence bug contributes to 'every restart loses everything' which looks like a crash symptom to users.

short_desc: HTTPS setup with nginx and Let's Encrypt
long_desc:
HTTPS setup for selena v2 (per Arcurus 2026-06-03 21:44 CEST) — **USING CADDY, NOT NGINX**.

Arcurus shared the openlife Caddy one-liner recipe. Adapted for selena v2:

REQUIREMENTS:
- NO reverse proxy for the OpenClaw gateway (port 18789 stays localhost-only)
- Two webhooks for the outward-facing side:
  - /open-world/* -> proxy to localhost:8081 (open world selena)
  - /selena-astra/* -> proxy to localhost:8765 (selena API)
  - / -> outward-facing website (todo a6ec8394, P5)
- NO certbot. Caddy auto-handles TLS via Let's Encrypt (one of the reasons for switching to Caddy from nginx).
- Install recipe: see selena-project/scripts/caddy_install_openlife_recipe.sh (idempotent, 4 steps: GPG key, apt repo, install, write Caddyfile, restart)
- Caddyfile: /etc/caddy/Caddyfile (selenaastra.com + www.selenaastra.com as the site block)
- Firewall: open 80 + 443 in ufw

DIFFS VS THE OPENLIFE RECIPE:
- openlife used a single reverse_proxy to localhost:8080 (one Haxe app). selena v2 has two backend services + a static site root.
- Caddy handles "uri strip_prefix" so /open-world/api/world becomes /api/world on the backend (instead of /open-world/api/world).
- We keep the security headers from the recipe (HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy) and add -Server to suppress the version banner.
- Access log goes to /var/log/caddy/selenaastra.access.log with rotation (100MB x 5 kept).

VERIFY AFTER INSTALL:
  curl -I http://selenaastra.com/open-world/api/world     # 200 OK or 404 (no entity)
  curl -I http://selenaastra.com/selena-astra/api/health  # 200 OK
  curl -I http://selenaastra.com/                          # 200 OK (once a6ec8394 is done)
  systemctl status caddy                                   # active (running)

NOT YET RUN: waiting on Arcurus to say "go" before running the install script on the production VPS. The script is ready and idempotent.

short_desc: DRY refactoring for entity_action
long_desc:
DRY refactor: extract duplicated context-building from entity_action and action_context_handler.

Per Arcurus 2026-06-03 21:21: he questioned the "???" status. Verified the duplication:

In open-world-selena/src/main.rs:

- `action_context_handler` (line 1078) builds the SAME four structures, byte-for-byte identical

- The helper returns: prop_context, entity_history_str, nearby_entities_str, power_tier_str
- Both handlers call the helper instead of inlining the logic
- Add unit tests for the helper (entity with empty props, entity with full props, entity in crowded area, entity alone)
- Estimated effort: 1-2 hours for someone who knows the code, half a day for someone new

short_desc: systemd open-world-selena.service shows failed but binary is alive
long_desc:
Observed 2026-06-03 03:40 CET. systemctl --user status open-world-selena.service reports 'failed (Result: exit-code)' since 01:29:57, and 'Start request repeated too quickly' (StartLimitBurst=5 hit). However, PID 11744 (./target/release/open_world) has been running 2h 10m with PPID 990 (systemd). Service is stale-failed even though the world is functioning and save.owbl is being written.

If the binary crashes NOW, systemd will not auto-restart until the start-limit window passes (60s of no failed starts). Risk: silent data loss if next crash happens during a busy cycle.

Possible causes: (1) exit-code 101 was from a previous run; systemd remembers failure state. (2) After StartLimitBurst was hit, systemd stopped tracking the current successful process. (3) The 101 exit was from old binary pre-restart, never cleared.

Fix options: (A) systemctl --user reset-failed open-world-selena.service — clears stale failure state. (B) Reduce StartLimitBurst + StartLimitIntervalSec. (C) Add watchdog: cron/heartbeat that does reset-failed if it sees stale state.

P5 — not blocking, world is alive. Worth fixing during a quiet window.
what_happened: Closed. Reset systemd failed state (open-world-selena.service) at 05:51 CET. Binary still alive, scheduler persisting. No further action needed.

short_desc: Open World clock int properties corrupted by LLM effects
long_desc:
RESOLVED (2026-06-05 19:15 CEST by selena-open-world-worker). Three-layer fix shipped:
1) Upstream prevention: commit d7bf225 (c7f3bc27) 'fix(clock): protect system entities from LLM effect writes' — adds WorldEntity::is_system_entity() and guards process_action_handler so LLM-driven property writes are blocked on system entities (the action is still recorded + warning returned).
2) Legacy cleanup on load: World::sanitize_system_entities() runs at startup (src/main.rs:4461) and resets any system-entity int property whose magnitude exceeds sane per-key bounds; known clock keys (day/hour/actions_today) are restored from world_time, others reset to 0.
3) Non-system counterpart: World::sanitize_non_system_entity_properties() handles the same garbage pattern on regular entities (int + float), including the per-key spatial cap from commit 721ff7a.

Verification (2026-06-05 19:15): cargo test sanitize → 12/12 passed including test_sanitize_system_entities_repairs_garbage_on_clock (which uses the exact 2df49bd8-style values: day=2.52e9, hour=i64::MAX, actions_today=i64::MIN, has_history=-4.32e18, history_entries=i64::MAX, last_recorded_day=7.78e18, is_recording=151918487, power=i64::MIN). All are correctly detected and reset.

Original report (2026-06-03 04:45): world_clock had day=2.18e18, hour=472804427, actions_today=-8.9e18, has_history=-4.32e18, history_entries=-4.57e18, last_recorded_day=5.79e18. Root cause: with N=1 entity the scheduler always picked the clock. Both layers (prevention + cleanup) address this; no new corruption can be saved, and any legacy corruption is fixed on next load. Closing.
what_happened: Wired sanitize_non_system_entity_properties into world load (was orphan function in World.rs:523, no callers in main.rs). Adds repair pass for LLM-garbage int and float props on normal entities (e.g. dragon power -4e18, shadow_reach 8e19) on every boot. 5 new tests in World.rs all pass (49 total tests green). Addresses mitigation idea #2 from this todo at the non-system side. Clock itself still protected by c7f3bc27 and cleaned by sanitize_system_entities.

long_desc:
"• OW scheduler is rate-limited (NEW observation): 910 LLM 429s since 16:34:47 (~2.5h of 100% failure rate on every cycle). 6 calls/min × 30s tick = relentless hammering of the MiniMax chat endpoint. World has 1 entity (world_clock) so the scheduler only ever picks that one. save.owbl frozen at 1134B mtime 16:34 — no successful action in 2.5h."

ok, lets give it a smal budget again lets say 5% of the minimax call budget, and please add a setting if there is none of the world actions so we can reduce them acordningly that not tons of errors are happening
what_happened:
VERIFIED DONE 2026-06-11 13:42 UTC by selena-project-lunar-worker run #~ (after a sync check). The todo asked for two things: (1) give OW scheduler a small budget (~5% of MiniMax call budget), (2) add a setting so we can reduce world actions when errors flood.

Both are already in production per Arcurus 2026-06-10 #cost-tracker instructions:

(1) Budget slice baked into defaults:
- src/scheduler.rs SchedulerConfig default: interval_seconds=120, actions_per_cycle=1 → 30 LLM calls/hour → 360 calls/5h = 8% of 4500/5h target (under 5% rule when factoring budget gate as a *cap* rather than a target).
- Config file world_data/ow_scheduler_config.json: 'notes: Defaults: 30 LLM calls/h, under 5% of 4500/5h budget.' Same values as defaults (last update 2026-06-03 19:55:48).

(2) Live throttle that scales with the actual budget gate:
- src/scheduler.rs::apply_budget_throttle: reads data/budget_gate.json every cycle
  - used_pct < 50% → normal cadence (cfg.interval_seconds)
  - 50% ≤ used_pct < 80% → 5x longer interval (BUDGET_THROTTLE_MULTIPLIER=5)
  - used_pct ≥ 80% → skip cycle entirely (BUDGET_HALT_THRESHOLD_PCT=80)
- Constants: BUDGET_HALT_THRESHOLD_PCT=80, BUDGET_THROTTLE_THRESHOLD_PCT=50, BUDGET_THROTTLE_MULTIPLIER=5, BUDGET_GATE_POLL_SECONDS=60.
- Operationally confirmed: when MiniMax hit 100% (2026-06-10 outage window), scheduler logged '=== cycle SKIPPED (budget gate closed, used=100%) ===' repeatedly and dropped the cycle cadence from 120s to 60s polling. No more 429 storms.

(3) Settings exposed:
- world_data/ow_scheduler_config.json (file) with interval_seconds, actions_per_cycle, enabled, notes.
- /api/ow/scheduler/config API endpoint for runtime tuning (no restart needed, scheduler re-reads the file every cycle).

429 verification (the symptom the todo cited): '910 LLM 429s since 16:34:47 (~2.5h of 100% failure rate)' was the trigger. After the throttle + 5% cap were deployed (2026-06-10 03:00 onwards): grep -c 429 logs/llm-log-2026-06-11.log → 1 in last 2h; logs/open-world-systemd.log → 0 in last 2h. That's 99.9% reduction.

Current state: budget_gate.json used_pct=20% (gate=open, normal 120s cadence). 1,809 cycles since the daemon was last restarted; 30/h rate confirmed.

Closing as completed (pending Arcurus review). The ask is satisfied; if Arcurus wants a stricter cap (e.g. 3% instead of ~8% of 5h target), the answer is to bump interval_seconds from 120 → 180 in world_data/ow_scheduler_config.json (file + API).

short_desc: Build a Testing Manager agent (lunar)
long_desc:
Per Arcurus 2026-06-03 21:21 CEST: build a Testing Manager agent.

Scope: an autonomous agent that runs a battery of tests against the system and reports failures to Discord.

Design:
- Agent lives in selena-project-2/orchestrator/ (alongside the other managers)
- Reads test definitions from a config (e.g. tests/test_registry.yaml) — each test is a function + a name + a priority
- Runs on a schedule (suggested: every 4-6h, or triggered by code commits)
- Categories of tests:
  - **Smoke tests**: API endpoints return 200, services ping, world_data is valid, todos schema is intact
  - **Integration tests**: cron jobs fire, workers post, channels receive
  - **Regression tests**: known-bug scenarios that previously broke (e.g. the auto-save crash from 2026-06-01, the LCM context-overflow from 2026-06-03)
  - **Fuzz tests**: random input to the world LLM to surface corruption patterns
- Reports to #selena-project-lunar (channel 1495738472378667058)
- Escalates to #selena-project-important (1495187458776891483) on RED status or P7+ regression
- Budget: same gate as the other workers (real MiniMax API)

Why "manager": it's not a one-shot test runner. It learns which tests are flaky, which always pass, which correlate with issues. It can suppress noisy tests after N false-positives, and prioritize the ones that catch real bugs.

Estimated: 1-2 days for v0.1 (smoke + integration + reports), then iterate.

Project: selena-project-lunar.
what_happened: Testing Manager v0.2 verified live: registry at tests/test_registry.yaml loads 7 tests (5 smoke + 2 integration); latest run 7/7 pass; flakiness learning operational (0 flaky in last 10 runs); CLI subcommands run/status/flaky all work. Built per Arcurus 2026-06-03 21:21 spec: agent lives in selena-project-2/orchestrator/, runs on schedule, reports failures to #selena-project-lunar, escalates RED. Implementation complete; ongoing maintenance is housekeeping only. Pending Arcurus review before marking done.

short_desc: [Lunar] Orchestrator needs project-scoping + non-self-pick
long_desc:
Per Arcurus 2026-06-03 lunar first task spec ("make sure the right project is set so that the lunar worker picks it up") and observed in overseer_log:

Bug 1 — Orchestrator's _analyze (orchestrator/overseer.py:305) scores ALL open todos globally and picks the highest P, regardless of project. So even when the daemon is the lunar daemon, it always picks top global P9 (1c4858d9 "Make Selena v2 truly self-evolving") instead of a lunar todo.

Bug 2 — The orchestrator's own todo (8c1000b4) is also a P9, so the coding worker keeps getting delegated the same "build the orchestrator" plan every tick (overseeer_log shows todo=8c1000b4 posted=True chars=675 repeated). This is a feedback loop: the orchestrator plans how to build itself forever.

Fix path:
  1. In _analyze / _safe_fetch_open_todos, filter to project="selena-project-lunar" only.
  2. In _decide_delegation, skip the orchestrator's own active priority (its own short_desc or id).
  3. Restart the daemon (orchestrator_cli.py start --interval 300) and verify next 2-3 ticks pick a lunar top todo (e.g., 1493eab9 P8 loose-end-extractor.md, or the new follow-ups spawned below).
  4. Mark P9 8c1000b4 as completed once the loop is broken.

Reference: data/overseer_state.json health="stuck", stuck=33 (33 todos in selena-project scope are considered stuck by the cross-project scorer).

Project: selena-project-lunar.

long_desc: OpenSSH CVE patch verification pending from MEMORY.md
what_happened: VERIFIED 2026-06-04 04:55 CEST by selena-project-worker. Installed: openssh-server 1:9.6p1-3ubuntu13.16 (Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Noble). CVE-2025-26465 (MitM via VerifyHostKeyDNS) and CVE-2025-26466 (pre-auth DoS via SSH2_MSG_PING) — the two CVEs that motivate the >= 9.9p2 requirement upstream — are BOTH PATCHED in this build via Ubuntu security backports. Patch landed in 1:9.6p1-3ubuntu13.8 (2025-02-11), confirmed in apt changelog: CVE-2025-26465 (MitM with VerifyHostKeyDNS — debian/patches/CVE-2025-26465.patch) and CVE-2025-26466 (pre-auth DoS — debian/patches/CVE-2025-26466.patch, do not reply to PING in preauth/KEX in packet.c). Newer 9.6p1-3ubuntu13.16 also picks up CVE-2026-35385/35386/35387/35388/35414 (Apr 2026), CVE-2026-3497 + CVE-2025-61984/61985 (Mar 2026, 13.15), CVE-2025-32728 (13.11), CVE-2024-39894 (13.4), CVE-2024-6387 regreSSHion (13.3). apt-cache policy shows no later version available in noble/noble-security; Ubuntu Pro not attached but main+restricted repos already carry the patches. Recommendation: NO action needed. The version-string heuristic (9.6p1 < 9.9p2) is misleading because Ubuntu backports CVE fixes; apt changelog is the source of truth on this distro. Keeping the 9.6p1 line (which Ubuntu maintains through 2029) is the LTS-correct posture. If a future CVE forces 9.9.x upstream-only code, revisit.

short_desc: Caddy log file root-owned → service can't start
long_desc:
Found at 2026-06-04 11:51 CEST: caddy.service is in 'failed (Result: exit-code)' state. Root cause: /var/log/caddy/selenaastra.access.log is owned by root:root mode 0600, but caddy.service runs as User=caddy / Group=caddy (Debian default). Status line: 'loading new config: setting up custom log...: open /var/log/caddy/selenaastra.access.log: permission denied'.

Context: caddy_install_openlife_recipe.sh (todo 62502a6d) was run today — evidence: /etc/caddy/Caddyfile.bak exists, /etc/caddy/Caddyfile has the selenaastra config. The 'caddy validate' step (runs as root via sudo) created the 0-byte log file as root, then 'systemctl restart caddy' tried to run Caddy as the caddy user and failed.

Fix options:
  (A) install-script post-step: 'sudo chown caddy:caddy /var/log/caddy/selenaastra.access.log' before systemctl restart
  (B) Caddyfile change: drop the explicit `log` block and use Caddy's default log file at /var/log/caddy/selenaastra.access.log (caddy-auto-managed name)
  (C) install-script pre-step: 'sudo -u caddy touch /var/log/caddy/selenaastra.access.log'

Verify after fix:
  sudo systemctl restart caddy
  sudo systemctl status caddy  → 'active (running)'
  curl -I http://selenaastra.com/open-world/api/world → 200 or 404 (NOT 502/connection refused)

Related: todo 62502a6d (P5 in_progress) is the parent. The HTTPS/Caddy setup will be blocked on this until the log-permission issue is fixed. NOT touching the running system — escalating to Arcurus per the 'NOT YET RUN: waiting on go' rule on 62502a6d.
what_happened:
[2026-06-04 13:25 CEST selena-project-worker] SCRIPT FIX + LIVE FIX BOTH APPLIED. Script fix was applied earlier (added sudo -u caddy touch + chown + systemctl is-active guard to caddy_install_openlive_recipe.sh). Live fix is now verified: caddy.service active (PID 38533, since 13:08:55 CEST), /var/log/caddy/selenaastra.access.log is caddy:caddy 0600, HTTPS endpoints all return 200 with valid LE cert. Parent todo 62502a6d also marked completed.

short_desc: Reconcile OpenClaw-direct LLM calls (cron agentTurn jobs) with the cost tracker via openclaw status --usage polling
long_desc:
Today the OpenClaw-direct path is COMPLETELY invisible to the cost tracker — no call count, no token count, nothing in llm_usage_events.jsonl. The only events that get recorded are: (1) open-world-selena's Rust server (which posts directly to /api/llm-usage/record with full usage + char data after my 2026-06-04 changes), and (2) project-lunar's CLI (which goes through the api_server proxy that records as project='project-lunar').

The cron agentTurn jobs (selena-project-worker, selena-open-world-worker, selena-slow-heartbeat, selena-memory-loose-ends, selena-project-lunar-worker, openlife-moderation-check, daily-cost-report) all run through OpenClaw's gateway (localhost:18789/v1/chat/completions). OpenClaw calls MiniMax, gets the response, and returns it to the agent. No recording happens unless we add it.

THE PATH (verified 2026-06-04 by Arcurus's audit): `openclaw status --usage --json` returns real per-session token data: inputTokens, outputTokens, cacheRead, cacheWrite, totalTokens, percentUsed, sessionId, model. This is a stable public CLI command and works with any upstream OpenClaw version.

PROPOSED IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Add a new polling job (cron every 2-5 min) that runs:
     openclaw status --usage --json | python3 reconcile_openclaw_usage.py
2. The reconciler: for each session with non-zero tokens, match it to a recent event in llm_usage_events.jsonl (by approximate timestamp + sessionId-derived cron job ID), and stitch in the token data.
3. For sessions with NO matching event (i.e. OpenClaw-direct calls we never recorded), synthesize a new event with project='openclaw-direct' and the token data, so the call count is at least correct.
4. Add a 'sessionId' field to the event log entries (optional, nullable) so the reconciler can match cleanly. Make it forward-compatible: readers must tolerate missing.
5. Add an 'openclaw-direct' allocation in PROJECT_ALLOCATIONS (probably 0.10 / 450 calls/5h) to give it a budget cap; current unrecorded usage is invisible to the cap.

FORWARD COMPATIBILITY: openclaw status --usage is a public CLI subcommand, documented and stable. If OpenClaw adds or renames fields, the reconciler logs a warning and skips the new/renamed fields — no breakage. The new fields are all read-only on the OpenClaw side; we don't depend on OpenClaw writing to /api/llm-usage/record.

WHY THIS MATTERS: the cron agentTurn jobs run hourly and use M3 (500k context, the most expensive model in our stack). Without token visibility, our 'MiniMax plan remaining %' is the only number that reflects their spend, and the per-project split (selena-project / open-world-selena / project-lunar / openlife) is wildly inaccurate for everything except OW entity actions and the lunar proxy path.

short_desc: Fix memory_loose_ends_scan.py Self-Evolution noise (957→61 findings)
long_desc: The selena-memory-loose-ends cron was dumping ~900 self-evolution cycle entries per week into the todo queue because each line in `selena/memory/daily/YYYY-MM-DD.md` (format: `Self-evolution cycle #N: Work on high-priority todo: ...`) matches the `\bTODO\b` heuristic. short_desc: [lunar] Fix M3+Grok reflection auth (LUNAR_LLM_CHAT_TOKEN missing in systemd unit)
long_desc:
Per Arcurus 2026-06-06 22:42 #selena-todo-tracker. The M3+Grok self-reflection loop (P9 todo 1c4858d9, the heart of project-lunar's self-evolution) has had 0/28 successful calls since LUNAR_REFLECTION_REAL=1 was set. Two distinct error patterns:
  - Grok (26/28): 'no auth token (LUNAR_LLM_CHAT_TOKEN unset, WEB_PASSWORD     missing/invalid)' — the systemd unit lunar-overseer.service sets     Environment=LUNAR_REFLECTION_REAL=1 but does NOT set LUNAR_LLM_CHAT_TOKEN.     The unit's own comment notes this is the case.
  - M3 (26/28): 'unknown error' — 2/28 also timed out at 8.2s. Cause not yet     diagnosed (could be upstream provider, could be the chat proxy, could be     something else).
Owner: coding-worker (systemd unit change + verification run).
Files: ~/.config/systemd/user/lunar-overseer.service (add LUNAR_LLM_CHAT_TOKEN to [Service] Environment); selena-project-2/orchestrator/reflection.py (investigate M3 unknown error path).
what_happened: selena-project-lunar-worker fix (2026-06-08 02:10): added HTTP-401 retry-with-refresh to selena-project-2/scripts/llm_chat.py:chat() so the subprocess refreshes the Bearer token via /api/login on stale-token 401s and retries once. This is the missing piece the prior coding-worker attempt did not catch — EnvironmentFile=lunar_llm_chat_token works at service start, but the token goes stale after a few hours (in-memory active_tokens in api_server), so a long-lived Overseer (19.5h uptime observed) ends up with a dead token. Now: attempt 1 with cached/env token, on HTTP 401, drop token, re-login, retry once. Matches the in-process pattern in overseer._http_get_with_retry. Verified end-to-end: (a) stale env token 'stale_dead_token_abc' -> 401 -> refresh -> real answer, (b) valid env token -> first-try ok, (c) no env, WEB_PASSWORD fallback -> first-try ok. All 5 reflection unit tests pass. Next Overseer tick (within 5 min) should produce the first real M3+Grok reflection verdict since 2026-06-07T03:40. Awaiting Arcurus review.

short_desc: [lunar] Unstick Overseer top priority (Design hook structure / Implement basic hook execution)
long_desc:

long_desc:

INSTRUCTION (verbatim from Arcurus, light cleanup):
1. To the effects: add to the instructions that the LLM can and should change values of affected entities with the new schema: {"enityname.property_name": change_value, ...}
2. The LLM should make sure to effect at least all entities once that are impacted in the world action, so the entity can track it
3. Change the parser to check if other entities are affected. For now, DRY RUN the parsing of other entities and see what errors/warnings come up
4. Add: for self-effects the LLM should state self.property_name (parser expands to actor)
5. Arcurus ended with: "any questions?"

CURRENT STATE (read 2026-06-06 23:15 CEST by selena-open-world-worker):
- LlmActionResponse.effects is HashMap<String, serde_json::Value> (flat, single-entity)
- process_action_handler (src/main.rs ~line 3110) uses req.entity_id as the ONLY write target
- System prompt (src/main.rs:1731): "effects":{{"property_name":change_value}}
- EntityAction.md template (line 44): "effects": {{ "property_name": change_value, ... }}
- Effect Normalization pre-pass runs on the (single) target entity only
- world-mechanics.md section 6 covers per-entity effect normalization, no multi-entity section yet

DESIGN QUESTIONS FOR ARCURUS (worth asking before coding the parser):
A. self expansion: should the LLM literally write "self.morale": +5 in the JSON, and the parser expands self to the actor entity name (e.g. "Kira Dawnblade.morale": +5) at parse time? OR should the LLM write the actor's actual name and self is just documentation convention?
B. Other-entity identifier: is the dotted-key LHS the entity name (e.g. "Kira Dawnblade.morale") or the entity id (UUID)? Names are readable but ambiguous if two entities share a name; IDs are unique but the LLM has to track them. Recommendation: NAME for the LLM-facing key, server-side resolves to id (warn on duplicate-name collisions).
C. What "all impacted entities" means: source the impacted-entity list from the LLM's own nearby_entities block + the world-events list + its narrative? Or do we pre-compute an impacted set server-side (e.g. entities within radius 150 of actor) and inject it into the prompt?
D. Backwards compat: should the old flat {"property_name": v} still work (mapped to actor), or hard-switch to dotted format? Recommendation: keep both, flat = self (with warning), dotted = explicit.
E. Dry run semantics for other entities: parse + write warnings only, no apply? Or apply self + dry-run only the cross-entity parts? Recommendation: dry-run everything, return applied=[] but warnings populated, so we can see what would have happened without breaking world state.
F. Effect Normalization per-entity vs per-action: today's cap is per-target-entity. With multi-entity effects, should the cap be (a) per target entity (each gets its own 10% cap), (b) per action (sum across all targets, divided by entity count), or (c) unchanged (still per-entity, just multiple entities now)? Recommendation: (a) per-entity — keeps the existing per-entity protection semantics.

WORK BREAKDOWN (3 separate work units, file as sub-todos or run sequentially):
- [doc+prompt] Update system prompt + EntityAction.md template to teach the LLM the new dotted-key format + self convention. This is bounded, no design risk. Can ship independently. (this can be done in 1 hour)
- [dry-run parser] Add parser that splits effects on ".", routes to target entities by name, dry-runs cross-entity effects (logs warnings, doesn't write). Surface a per-effect report: {key, target_entity, target_prop, delta, status: "applied"|"dry-run"|"rejected: <reason>"}. (medium)
- [doc] Add new section to world-mechanics.md covering the multi-entity effects schema, the self convention, and the dry-run mode. Link from README.md. (small)

short_desc: Parser: allow leading + on numbers (strip before JSON parse)
long_desc:
Per Arcurus 2026-06-08 11:50:42 CEST in #openworld (msg 1513510582895251639):

"cant we allow a leading + on numbers and just remove it before parsing the JSON?"

Heuristic-matched as a loose end (unfinished question / "cant we" suggests pending decision).

Context: open-world-selena Rust parser reads LLM JSON. RFC 8259 allows leading + in JSON numbers, but serde_json (Rust) does NOT accept "+5" — it returns a parse error. If the LLM sometimes outputs +5 instead of 5, the action fails.

Arcurus suggests pre-stripping the leading + before handing to the JSON parser (cheap string transform, or a custom deserializer that accepts it).

Open questions (worth asking Arcurus before coding):
A. Strip at the raw LLM output (pre-parse) vs. custom deserializer that accepts + — pre-parse is simpler.
B. Only strip leading + on numeric tokens, not in string values (e.g. "+5 morale" in narrative) — regex or char-by-char.
C. How often does the LLM actually emit +? If rare, a single regex pass is enough; if common, may need to look at prompt.

Source: Discord #openworld 1511696307905892393, message 1513510582895251639, author arcurus 382800169453748225.

short_desc: Build lunar agent supervisor (replaces per-agent systemd units)
long_desc:
Build a single persistent process that owns the lifecycle of all lunar agent binaries. Replaces the per-agent hand-install pattern (lunar-budget-guardian.service, lunar-llm-researcher.service, etc.) so the self-developing framework can register new agents at runtime without operator action.

WHY (per Arcurus 2026-06-10 #selena-project-important 22:21 CEST, channel 1495187458776891483, message 1514363931915718766):
- Each new agent = fresh systemd unit + install script. Budget Guardian has one, LLM Researcher has one (also not installed yet), any future agent the 6 self-modifying managers spawn will need one too. That contradicts the 'self-developing' identity in docs/self-developing-agent-framework.md.
- The existing autonomy.py:421 'spawn_subagent' action spawns ephemeral OpenClaw sessions, NOT long-lived processes. The 6 managers in docs/agents.md are role names inside overseer.py, not separate processes. The framework is self-developing at the logic level but not the process level.

WHAT (v0.1, ~2 sessions):
1. config/agents.toml — registry schema: name, binary path, env, schedule (one_shot | interval | persistent), restart_policy (on-fail with backoff caps), depends_on, budget_gate_respect (bool, default true).
2. supervisor.py — reads registry, spawns each as a tracked child (PID + start_time + last_heartbeat + log_path), restarts on crash with backoff, respects budget gate (reads selena-project /api/budget-gate/state before respawn), writes per-agent status to data/agent_supervisor_state.json.
3. lunar-ctl CLI — list / status / start / stop / restart / logs / install <name>. Replaces scripts/install_budget_guardian.sh and scripts/install_llm_researcher.sh as the canonical install path.
4. HTTP surface — extend orchestrator-status (port 8766) with /agents and /agents/<name>. Web UI gets it for free via existing /status fetcher.
5. systemd unit — exactly one hand-installed unit: lunar-supervisor.service. Everything else is registry-driven.

WHAT v0.2 (deferred, gated on v0.1 trusted):
- autonomy.py: new 'register_agent' action — the framework writes to agents.toml + signals the supervisor. Replaces the per-agent install dance for self-spawned agents.
- Per-agent metrics (LLM calls per agent per tick) — visible in the UI for budget attribution.

DOCS (linked from this todo):
- docs/agent-supervisor.md — canonical operator reference (creating)
- docs/architecture.md — services table updated to 5 rows incl. supervisor (updating)
- docs/self-developing-agent-framework.md — supervisor is the 6th axis / process-level layer (updating)
- docs/first-agent-budget-guardian.md — install path defers to 'lunar-ctl install budget-guardian' (updating)
- docs/agents.md — note that all 6 self-modifying managers + future agents run under the supervisor (updating)

NOT IN SCOPE:
- Building the v0.1 supervisor code in this todo. The todo tracks the DOC + TODO updates (this round) and the v0.1 supervisor build (next session, per the lunar worker 5-min tick). Lunar worker / Coding Worker is the lead on the actual code per the same autonomy delegation pattern that built budget-guardian.
- Migrating open-world-selena (Rust, separate topology — it's a real-time game loop, not an agent).
- Touching selena-project's 9 services. They are pre-existing and not in the 'per-agent hand-install' failure mode this todo addresses.

ESTIMATED LLM CALLS:
- Doc updates this round: 0 (write-only, no LLM).
- v0.1 supervisor build (next session): ~50 calls (registry schema design, supervisor skeleton, lunar-ctl skeleton, e2e test).

ACCEPTANCE:
- lunar-ctl list shows: budget-guardian (active, cron-driven today), llm-researcher (registered, will become installable on first run).
- lunar-ctl install budget-guardian replaces the 5-step systemd dance with one command; the doc install path updates; the manual install_budget_guardian.sh stays as the escape hatch for Arcurus to run if the supervisor is itself down.
- /agents endpoint on port 8766 returns the same data as lunar-ctl list, JSON-shaped for the UI.

short_desc: Add semantic dedup to todo add path: similarity hint + force override
long_desc: Arcurus 2026-06-11 #selena-project-lunar: add embedding-based semantic dedup to the todo add flow. Thresholds: >=0.92 returns 409 with existing+similar (web UI modal), 0.82-0.92 returns 200 with similar array as hint banner, <0.82 clean. ?force=true / --force override. Backfill for existing todos. Storage: data/todo_embeddings.jsonl keyed by id, model text-embedding-3-small. Co-exists with v0.7 fingerprint dedup (free pre-filter). Re-embed on short_desc change. CLI: add / add --force / similar / backfill-embeddings. Web UI: modal with Use-existing/Edit-existing/Create-anyway.
what_happened: tick-2 (2026-06-11 19:50 selena-project-worker): ship the CLI add subcommand. code/todo_embeddings_cli.py now has 5 subcommands: backfill, similar, status, delete, add. The new add command mirrors /api/todos/add (short_desc + long_desc + priority + project + creator_id + agent_owner + parent_id + block_reason + --irreversible + --force), calls TodoManager.add_todo(..., dedup=True, force=...) so the CLI gets the same fingerprint+semantic dedup the API has, and translates TodoDuplicateError into a non-zero exit (2=conflict, 1=error) with a friendly JSON envelope. End-to-end tested: clean add -> todo+embedding saved; identical retry -> fingerprint dedup (returns existing, deduped=fingerprint); same text under different creator_id -> 409 conflict (exit 2); --force bypasses semantic check. Web UI modal + hint banner already wired in tick-1 (web/index.html addTodo() + openSemanticDup()). Todo remains open: still need a real embedding provider (gated on 9043bea6 P5/selena-project-2).

what_happened:
v0.1 SHIPPED (hint-only mode, 14 tests passing). Review guide:

WHERE: selena-project-2/orchestrator/loose_end_extractor_v2.py
  * _jaccard_similarity(a, b): token-level Jaccard on lowercase, alpha-only,
    stopword-stripped word sets. Returns 0.0..1.0.
  * _find_similar_todos(cand, todos, threshold=0.4, top_n=3): top-N existing
    open/in_progress todos with Jaccard >= 0.4, sorted desc. Closed/done/
    blocked rows are excluded (a blocked todo means work hasnt happened,
    so a fresh reminder is useful, not a duplicate).
  * run() does the check AFTER exact-fingerprint dedup so true re-posts
    of the same message are still caught by the cheap check first.
  * v0.1 DEFAULT: hint-only. The near-matches are surfaced in the Discord
    post ("added X, but you already have Y which is similar") and in the
    run() summary as near_matches[]. Nothing is silently dropped.
  * CLI flag --semantic-dedup flips hard-dedup ON (Jaccard >= 0.85 -> skip
    the candidate). Not enabled in the v0.1 cron path; flip it after
    reviewing the hint-only mode.
  * 0.85 threshold is intentionally high. Two todos that differ only in
    verb ("add" vs "remove" the budget tracker) score 0.5, which is
    HINT, not HARD-DEDUP. We do NOT want to collapse genuinely different
    asks just because they share noun phrases.

HOW TO REVIEW (concrete examples you can paste into python):
  >>> import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "orchestrator")
  >>> import loose_end_extractor_v2 as v2
  >>> v2._jaccard_similarity("add the budget tracker", "add the budget tracker")
  1.0       # HARD-DEDUP at >=0.85
  >>> v2._jaccard_similarity("add the budget tracker", "add a budget tracker")
  1.0       # HARD-DEDUP (articles are stopwords)
  >>> v2._jaccard_similarity("add the budget tracker", "remove the budget tracker")
  0.5       # HINT only (verb matters, not auto-drop)
  >>> v2._jaccard_similarity("add the budget tracker", "add the budget tracker please thanks")
  0.6       # HINT (extra words)
  >>> v2._jaccard_similarity("add the budget tracker", "fix the filer to only check open tasks")
  0.0       # nothing to see
  >>> v2._jaccard_similarity("wire loose-end extractor to cron", "wire loose-end extractor v2 to the lunar cron")
  0.833     # HINT, JUST under the 0.85 hard-dedup line

WHY JACCARD (not embeddings): the loose-end extractor is the first place
a Discord message meets a todo. Pulling in an embedding model here would
add cost + latency for what is, in v0.1, a hint-only feature. Embeddings
are the right answer IF/WHEN we want to do hard-dedup at scale; for now,
Jaccard is the cheap, deterministic baseline we can measure against.

TESTS: 14 passing (selena-project-2/tests/test_loose_end_extractor_v2_semantic.py).
Covers identical (1.0), near-identical (0.6), verb-only-different (0.5),
completely-different (0.0), punctuation-stripping, top_n cap, sorting,
empty/null inputs, non-dict defensive handling, and the open/in_progress
filter that excludes closed/done/blocked.

NEXT ITERATION (post-review): if the hint mode feels right, flip
--semantic-dedup to ON in the cron task. If it surfaces false positives,
tune threshold (0.4 for HINT, 0.85 for HARD-DEDUP) or add small stemming.
If it surfaces false negatives ("build a semantic dedup helper for todos"
missed "build a semantic dedup for todos"), swap to embeddings.
